chk_problem.label: accurate
chk_problem.poster_evidence: Functional decline in older adults is typically recognized only after falls or observable gait impairment, closing the window for prevention. Routine biomarkers — already recorded but rarely analyzed longitudinally — may hold early warning signals. This study investigates whether temporal trajectories of 12 routine biomarkers can identify patients in the pre-clinical phase of mobility decline
chk_problem.reason: The poster accurately describes the problem of predicting pre-clinical functional mobility decline in older adults using longitudinal trajectories of routine biomarkers before falls or observable impairment occur.

chk_method.label: accurate
chk_method.poster_evidence: Twelve biomarkers were selected a priori based on pathophysiologic links to functional decline: hemoglobin, albumin, sodium, potassium, creatinine, HbA1c, vitamin D, RDW, CRP, BMI, systolic BP, diastolic BP. Trajectory features (slope, variability, delta, mean, count) were derived over a 3-year pre-index window. Models (LightGBM, XGBoost, Random Forest, Logistic Regression) were evaluated
chk_method.reason: The poster accurately details the feature engineering of trajectory descriptors from twelve biomarkers and modeling using LightGBM and other ML algorithms.

chk_data.label: accurate
chk_data.poster_evidence: We used the All of Us Controlled Tier Dataset (v8), selecting participants aged 50–125 with EHR data and at least one lab measurement. ... N = 297,861; 11.1% cases
chk_data.reason: The poster specifies the dataset (All of Us Controlled Tier Dataset v8) and the cohort size of 297,861 participants with 11.1% cases (approx. 33,062 cases).

chk_setup.label: accurate
chk_setup.poster_evidence: Models (LightGBM, XGBoost, Random Forest, Logistic Regression) were evaluated via 5-fold stratified CV with out-of-fold predictions.
chk_setup.reason: The poster correctly describes the evaluation setup using 5-fold stratified cross-validation with out-of-fold predictions comparing the four specified algorithms.

chk_primary_result.label: accurate
chk_primary_result.poster_evidence: Trajectory features significantly outperformed static summaries: AUROC 0.797 vs. 0.755 (DeLong p<0.001); AUPRC 0.380 vs. 0.304.
chk_primary_result.reason: The poster reports the primary quantitative findings for the trajectory model (AUROC of 0.797 and AUPRC of 0.380) and notes that it significantly outperformed static summaries.

chk_secondary_result.label: accurate
chk_secondary_result.poster_evidence: Prediction horizon analysis showed sustained discrimination 3–12 months before decline onset (AUROC 0.768–0.740).
chk_secondary_result.reason: The poster accurately presents the prediction horizon analysis results showing sustained prediction 3 to 12 months before onset with AUROCs ranging from 0.768 to 0.740.

chk_baseline.label: accurate
chk_baseline.poster_evidence: Trajectory features significantly outperformed static summaries: AUROC 0.797 vs. 0.755 (DeLong p<0.001); AUPRC 0.380 vs. 0.304. A 1:1 matched analysis confirmed independent trajectory signal (AUROC 0.727 vs. demographics-only 0.680).
chk_baseline.reason: The poster compares the trajectory model against both static laboratory summaries (AUROC 0.755, AUPRC 0.304) and demographics-only models (AUROC 0.680), satisfying both drafts of the reference.

chk_conclusion.label: accurate
chk_conclusion.poster_evidence: Longitudinal trajectory features from 12 routine biomarkers significantly outperform static summaries for predicting functional decline (AUROC 0.797 vs. 0.755; AUPRC 0.380 vs. 0.304; p<0.001). ... Because the model uses only measurements already ordered in routine care, it supports passive, zero-burden EHR integration for early detection of pre-clinical functional decline
chk_conclusion.reason: The poster's conclusion matches the reference, stating that longitudinal trajectory features significantly improve prediction and support passive, zero-burden EHR integration.

chk_limitation.label: accurate
chk_limitation.poster_evidence: Limitations: ICD-10 outcomes may miss objective decline; CRP and vitamin D have high missingness; no comorbidity adjustment. External validation and objective endpoints (e.g., gait speed) are needed.
chk_limitation.reason: The poster explicitly lists the limitations, including ICD-10 outcome definition issues, high missingness in CRP and vitamin D, lack of comorbidity adjustment, and the need for external validation.
